content_units: You already have a credible bridge into entry-level supply chain analyst work. Your strongest transferable assets are   inventory exposure, vendor coordination, scheduling, operational problem-solving, and Excel-based reporting  —all directly relevant to demand planning, replenishment, procurement ops, and logistics coordination roles.
9-month goal:   move from retail operations into an analyst-track role in Chicago with a target of   $65,000+  .
That target is   realistic  , especially for roles tied to inventory, replenishment, logistics analytics, procurement operations, or supply planning support.
Role   Why it fits your background   Likelihood at $65K+   Key skill gap to close
Supply Chain Analyst   Broad match for inventory, reporting, vendor coordination   High   SQL; stronger KPI storytelling
Inventory Analyst   Direct extension of cycle counts, stock accuracy, replenishment thinking   High   Forecasting metrics; ERP familiarity
Demand Planning Analyst Coordinator   Scheduling and inventory patterns translate well   Medium   Forecasting, seasonality, service-level logic
Logistics Analyst   Retail ops pace and exception handling are relevant   Medium-High   Transportation metrics; SQL; dashboarding
Procurement Analyst   Vendor communication is highly transferable   Medium-High   Spend analysis; PO/process knowledge
Replenishment Analyst   Strongest operational crossover from retail   High   Allocation/reorder point concepts
Operations Analyst   Broad operational analytics path if supply chain titles are limited   Medium-High   More structured business analysis examples
Option 1:   Inventory Analyst     Most direct match to inventory counts, shrink control, stock movement, and store-level operations   Fastest transition path
Option 2:   Replenishment Analyst     Strong fit if you can frame retail work around stock availability, replenishment timing, and vendor/service issues   Good chance of hitting compensation target
Option 3:   Supply Chain Analyst     Best long-term title growth and broadest opportunities across CPG, manufacturing, distribution, and retail   Requires stronger analytics proof points
Option 4:   Procurement Analyst     Vendor communication and issue resolution transfer well   Good alternative if analyst postings emphasize supplier reporting and PO tracking

Your priority is not “learn everything in supply chain.” It is to become   hireable for analyst interviews   by building evidence in four areas:   Excel depth, SQL, Power BI/business metrics, and supply chain concepts/ERP familiarity  .

Months 1-2   Reframe your foundation   Deepen Excel: XLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, pivots, Power Query, basic forecasting; learn core supply chain terms; rewrite resume bullets with metrics   Analyst-style resume v1 + 2 small Excel projects

Months 3-4   Build analytics credibility   Learn SQL basics to intermediate: SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, CASE, CTEs; improve Power BI with KPI dashboard design; study inventory metrics   Portfolio project: inventory dashboard + SQL case

Months 5-6   Specialize toward target roles   Focus on inventory, replenishment, logistics, and procurement workflows; learn common KPIs like fill rate, OTIF, stockout rate, inventory turnover, forecast accuracy   2 role-specific projects + tailored resume versions

Months 7-8   Start active job conversion   Apply in volume to Chicago roles; optimize LinkedIn; practice interview stories; network with local analysts, planners, and recruiters   50-80 targeted applications + mock interview bank
Month 9   Close offers   Refine salary positioning, improve case-study responses, intensify referrals, target contract-to-hire if needed   Offer-ready interview package
- Pivot tables, Power Query, nested IFs, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, text/date functions
- Build weekly inventory and vendor performance reports quickly
- This is the single most valuable gap to close for analyst credibility
- Aim to confidently query sales, inventory, shipment, and supplier tables
- Focus on DAX basics, filtering logic, trend visuals, KPI cards
- Even conceptual familiarity with SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or Blue Yonder helps
- You do not need mastery; you need to speak the workflow language
- Turn operational observations into concise recommendations
- Analyst hiring often depends on “Can this person explain what the numbers mean?”
What to learn later, not first
These can help later, but they are   not required   to land the first analyst role.
Resume Repositioning for Supply Chain Analyst Roles
You do not need to fake your background; you need to   translate it  .
Supply Chain / Inventory Analyst Candidate with 6 Years of Retail Operations Experience

Retail operations professional with 6 years of experience in inventory control, vendor coordination, workforce scheduling, and Excel-based reporting in high-volume environments. Experienced in identifying stock issues, maintaining operational accuracy, and supporting service-level performance. Currently building SQL and Power BI capability to transition into entry-level supply chain analyst, inventory analyst, or replenishment analyst roles in Chicago.
- Managed store operations and staff scheduling
- Analyzed staffing demand patterns and built schedules aligned to traffic, shipment timing, and service requirements.
- Executed and reconciled cycle counts, investigated inventory discrepancies, and supported on-shelf availability and stock accuracy goals.
- Coordinated with vendors on order timing, delivery issues, and discrepancy resolution to reduce stock interruptions.
- Produced Excel-based operational reports tracking sales trends, staffing needs, and inventory variances to support daily decision-making.
- Identified process inefficiencies in replenishment and task flow, contributing to improved in-stock execution and operational consistency.
- supported weekly volume of   $X sales / X SKUs / X deliveries
- cut reporting time by   X hours per week
- improved fill/in-stock performance by   X points
-   Core Skills:   Excel, Power BI, inventory analysis, vendor coordination, scheduling, KPI reporting, process improvement
-   Technical Skills:   Excel, Power BI, SQL in progress, ERP exposure if any
-   Projects:   2-3 mini analyst projects, even self-built
-   Relevant Coursework/Certificates:   only if practical and recent
- Deepen Excel until you can comfortably solve reporting tasks without templates
- Rewrite LinkedIn and resume around analyst keywords
Months 4-6: Create proof of analyst ability
- Build a Power BI dashboard using inventory or sales data
- Create one SQL project with joins and KPI outputs
- using data to fix process problems
- Be open to titles like   analyst coordinator  ,   inventory control analyst  , or   supply chain specialist   if compensation meets target or has a near-term path upward
Chicago Market Positioning and Pay Reality
For Chicago,   $65,000+   is most realistic if you target:
- supply chain analyst at larger firms
Less ideal for your pay target:
- buyer assistant roles without analytics scope
- pure coordinator jobs unless they are at large companies with strong pay bands
- Lead with your   6 years of operational experience
- Position yourself as   entry-level in title, not entry-level in business maturity
- This helps justify compensation above the lowest analyst band
